headline: Indonesia Ferry Capsizes in Java Sea; 6 Dead, 129 Missing
seoTitle: Indonesia Ferry Capsizes: 6 Dead, 129 Missing | FMB News
seoDescription: Indonesia's Virgo Transport 8 capsized in the Java Sea on September 13, leaving six confirmed dead, 108 rescued and 129 missing as search operations continue.
deck: Rescuers have saved 108 people from the Virgo Transport 8 after it capsized in rough Java Sea conditions; six deaths are confirmed and 129 people remain missing.
author: FMB News Desk
developingNote: This is a developing story. FMB News will update this report as verified information becomes available.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: At least six people have died and 129 remain missing after the Indonesian passenger ferry Virgo Transport 8 capsized in the Java Sea on Sunday, September 13, according to Indonesia's national search and rescue authorities.

The latest verified accounting says 108 people have been rescued. The vessel was carrying 243 people, including 30 crew members, while sailing from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan.
Indonesian authorities said the vessel encountered severe weather before contact was lost early Sunday. Search teams, ships and helicopters were deployed as rescuers worked in rough sea conditions.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Reuters, the Associated Press and Channel NewsAsia separately reported the latest rescue-agency figures of six confirmed deaths, 108 rescued people and 129 still missing.
Indonesia's Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said helicopter observations showed the vessel had capsized. The cause of the accident has not been determined and remains under investigation.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Virgo Transport 8 was traveling across the Java Sea between two of Indonesia's major islands when it lost contact. Indonesian rescue officials reported waves of roughly 2.5 to 3 meters in the area during the operation.
The ferry was also carrying vehicles. Authorities established a command center in Banjarmasin as families waited for verified passenger and survivor information.

Early official accounts differed on whether the vessel had fully sunk. Indonesia's search and rescue agency initially described it as sunk, while the transport minister later said aerial observation showed it capsized but had not sunk as of the afternoon. FMB News is therefore reporting only the verified fact that the vessel capsized.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The accident is a major maritime emergency within Southeast Asia, a region where island communities depend heavily on passenger ferries. It is relevant to Filipinos because the Philippines has similarly extensive inter-island travel and faces many of the same operational risks involving weather, vessel safety, passenger accounting and emergency response.

The disaster also comes days after the deadly MV June Aster ferry fire in the Philippines. The incidents are separate and there is no verified evidence linking their causes, but both underscore the importance of accurate manifests, rapid rescue coordination and transparent maritime investigations.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The exact cause of the capsizing has not been established.
Authorities have not issued a final determination on the vessel's physical status beyond confirmation that it capsized.
The casualty and missing-person counts may change as rescuers locate more people and reconcile passenger records.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for updated rescue numbers from Basarnas, confirmation of the vessel's condition, identification of victims, weather and sea-state assessments, and findings from Indonesia's transport-safety investigation.
FMB News will also watch for any confirmed Filipino nationals among those aboard. No such information was established in the verified sources reviewed for this report.

verificationNotes: The central event is confirmed by Indonesia's national search and rescue authorities and Transport Ministry reporting carried by ANTARA, Reuters, AP and CNA.
Reuters, AP and CNA independently corroborate the latest accounting of six dead, 108 rescued and 129 missing.
An earlier ANTARA/Basarnas update listed 140 missing before later rescue and accounting updates. The article uses the newer 129-missing figure corroborated by Reuters, AP and CNA.

Official descriptions differed over whether the ferry had sunk. The transport minister said helicopter observation showed it capsized but had not sunk as of the afternoon. FMB News therefore states only that the vessel capsized and flags the physical status as unresolved.
No cause is stated as fact. Severe weather is confirmed as the operating condition, while causation remains under investigation.
No Filipino casualties or passengers are claimed because none were established in the verified sources reviewed.
